hypothesis: a Gaussian-process emulator whose kernel is an isotropic RBF in the coordinates S x, with S the analytic sensitivity of the 15 far-end bus phase-voltage magnitudes to the 55 single-phase load P/Q injections, predicts far-end phase voltages of a three-phase unbalanced LV feeder more accurately than a standard stationary kernel, a graph-Laplacian kernel, and a tuned LinDistFlow baseline

transformer_convention.note: a first-order LinDistFlow operator cannot match a four-wire AC Jacobian exactly; the residual is the neutral/earth-return and second-order content, reported rather than hidden

row_permutation_is_noop.note: permuting the ROWS of S cannot change ||S(x-x')||; the max change in the pairwise feature norms is machine zero, which is why the archived row-permutation control returned an identical number

protocol_checks.title: the archived phase-label shuffle was a no-op
protocol_checks.detail: the archived control permuted the ROWS of the operator, and ||S(x-x')|| is invariant under row permutation, so that control returned an identical number by construction.  This artifact rebuilds the operator from a permuted LOAD->PHASE assignment, leaving the data on the real phases.

protocol_checks.title: the fixed-half test block is infeasible
protocol_checks.detail: 'train = n from one half, test = the other half' needs n + 110 <= 220 and fails at n = 160.  Redefined as a fixed 60-row test block with the training rows drawn from the remaining 160.  Scheme 1 folds here will NOT match another artifact that implemented the literal wording; scheme 0 is unaffected.

protocol_checks.title: normaliser undefined between two candidates
protocol_checks.detail: train-row per-output standard deviation is used everywhere. Paired MARGINS are invariant to this choice because the numerator and denominator share it; absolute RMSE values shift, so a margin comparison to an archived table is legitimate and an absolute-value comparison is not.

protocol_checks.title: 'effective rank at 2.6x' is vacuous and reserved
protocol_checks.detail: the operator takes no loading argument, so recomputing its own rank at another regime is an identity; and 2.6x is reserved evidence this artifact may not read.  Replaced with the data-whitened rank of S Cov(X_train) S^T and the injection-variance share captured by the top-6/11/20 row space of S, at 1.0x and 2.0x.

protocol_checks.title: the archived S_sheet15.npy is not elementwise comparable
protocol_checks.detail: that array came from a builder without the per-unit divide, without the |V| projection and with a real/imaginary split.  Support-pattern equality was required to proceed; the Frobenius difference, Pearson correlation and maximum principal angle are informational.

protocol_checks.title: LinDistFlow self-disagrees across prior artifacts
protocol_checks.measured: the 16-cell factorial test errors are in results/protocol_checks.json::baseline_sanity and in the per-fold table's b5_lindistflow.all_cells_rmse
protocol_checks.detail: order 1 vs 2 x flat vs no-load reference x target standardisation on/off x absolute vs scale-free penalty grid, selected by TRAIN-ONLY cross-validation; margins are reported against the selected cell AND against the legacy cell so the disagreement stays visible.

protocol_checks.title: two prior factual corrections not propagated
protocol_checks.detail: (i) the differential-mode share of far-end variance is re-measured here with the definition written out, and is reported as an argument FOR phase awareness rather than against it.  (ii) the phase-expanded admittance-weighted Laplacian is complex-SYMMETRIC, not Hermitian, so eigh/eigsh are invalid for it; both the Hermitian-part spectrum and the general spectrum are reported.

protocol_checks.title: two inherited operator errors found and fixed
protocol_checks.detail: (a) the Q-block sign: the archived builder wrote dV/dQ = +j dV/dP, which returns +Im(Z)/(Sb|V0|); the physical sign is -Im(Z)/(Sb|V0|).  (b) a missing factor 3 from the per-phase vs three-phase power base, which left the P block 3.15x low.  With both fixed, the P block matches the finite-difference AC Jacobian at correlation 0.995 and the implied effective resistance matches the path impedance to about 8 percent.  The kernel is scale-invariant in S, so (b) changes nothing for the treatment's metric but changes the LinDistFlow baseline's second-order term by 9x.

protocol_checks.title: marginal likelihood over-smooths on this target
protocol_checks.detail: the AC map is nearly linear in the pulled-back coordinates and has no observation noise, so the marginal likelihood's noise term absorbs model error and can prefer an over-smoothing lengthscale.  Both selection rules (marginal likelihood and train-only CV) are run over the SAME grid for EVERY candidate, and both are reported.

protocol_checks.title: the ridge baseline's intercept is mandatory
protocol_checks.detail: standardised features are zero-mean per column while the targets sit near 1.0 pu, so a no-intercept ridge returns a zero-mean prediction and a normalised RMSE of order 50.

pools.deliberate_exclusion: the unrestricted 55x55 Z-bus metric is NOT in the canonical pool because it is the full-state metric's load-restricted cousin; including it would let a same-object comparison suppress the treatment's margin.  It appears only in the mechanism section, where it is the point.

headline_claim.what_is_claimed: an isotropic RBF in the coordinates S x, with S the analytic sensitivity of the far-end phase-voltage magnitudes, is far more sample-efficient than a standard stationary kernel, a graph-Laplacian kernel, ridge, an MLP and a tuned LinDistFlow baseline on this feeder
headline_claim.what_is_NOT_claimed: that the OUTPUT RESTRICTION is what carries the kernel -- the mechanism factorial finds the unrestricted full-state operator at least as accurate on far-end targets from n = 40 upward
headline_claim.retained_claim: admittance structure helps, and the analytic zero-AC-solve operator is what supplies it

limitations: the bootstrap interval is over SPLITS, not over data: all folds share one 220-draw pool, so the genuinely independent evidence is the untouched regime and the untouched physically-moved-phase feeder, not the seed list

the physically-moved-phase control is NOT run here: it is reserved confirmation evidence for the survivor.  This artifact therefore cannot distinguish 'phase identity matters' from 'phase consistency matters'; the shuffled-label control here is the INCONSISTENCY test, not the identity test
the 2.6x stressed regime is reserved confirmation evidence and was never opened
the paper cannot claim a data-efficiency advantage over neural surrogates across the curve: the MLP is run at n = 80 only
S3 (ranking against the other candidates) is not evaluable inside this artifact
